Organic practices

Founded on family, grown on care

A farm that's been feeding Valley Center for a hundred years

Stehly Farms Organics began as a family farm in Valley Center, California, back in the 1920s. What started as one family's commitment to the land has passed down through generations — each one adding to the soil, the knowledge, and the responsibility that comes with growing food for a community.

In 2002, brothers Jerome and Noel Stehly took that legacy and reimagined it for a new era — shifting the farm fully toward organic, sustainable practices. Their goal wasn't just to grow produce. It was to build a farm that could feed the local community directly, season after season, while giving back to the land that made it possible.

Today, that same land grows the produce behind our CSA shares, our farm store, and everything else we do — still rooted in Valley Center, still family-run, still organic.

Why It's Different Here

Stewardship first, produce second

Everything on the farm — from how we plant to what we sell — is built around one idea: leave the land better than we found it, while feeding the people who count on us.

🌱

Sustainable Land Stewardship

Organic methods that protect the soil and water in Valley Center for the generations of Stehlys — and neighbors — still to come.

🧺

Direct to Community

CSA shares, a farm store, and seasonal offerings like turkeys and firewood — all built to get what the farm grows straight to local tables.

👨‍🌾

Family Run, Family Values

Jerome and Noel Stehly still run the operation their family started nearly a century ago — a farm, not a franchise.

More Than a Farm

A working farm you can actually visit

Beyond growing organic produce, the farm doubles as a gathering place — with event space rental set against the same fields that supply the CSA. It's a rare chance to bring people together on land that's been worked for a century.

Seasonal offerings like farm-raised turkeys and firewood round out what the land provides, all part of keeping the farm sustainable year-round — not just during peak harvest.
